title: Let the utility win with layers
prompt: The **Sold out** badge should be yellow (`#fde68a`) because it has the `.bg-accent` utility, but the component selector `.schedule .session-card .badge` out-scores it. Put the rules into cascade layers (`reset`, `components`, `utilities`, in that order) so utilities win. Keep every selector exactly as it is and don't use `!important`. The plain **Layout** badge must keep its lavender component style.
hints: Start the stylesheet with one statement that declares all three layer names in priority order.
Wrap each group of rules in `@layer name { … }`. Order inside the file doesn't matter once the statement fixes it.
`@layer reset, components, utilities;` then `@layer components { … }` and `@layer utilities { .bg-accent { … } }`.
explanation: The `@layer reset, components, utilities;` statement fixes the order, so any normal declaration in `utilities` beats any declaration in `components`, before specificity is compared. The badge selector keeps its (0,3,0) weight, which still matters inside the components layer, but it no longer competes with the utility. Leaving `.bg-accent` unlayered would also make it win, because unlayered styles beat layered ones, but naming the layer keeps the intent visible to the next person.

checks.utility-wins: The Sold out badge is yellow
checks.component-kept: The Layout badge keeps its lavender component style
